newsitem.title: INDIA: India budget tariff moves seen helping oil stocks.
newsitem.headline: India budget tariff moves seen helping oil stocks.

text.p: A broad hint by Indian Petroleum Minister T.R. Balu that oil import duties will be restructured in the 1997/98 budget to be announced later on Friday will be positive for oil stocks, sector analysts agreed.
The analysts expect the import tariff on crude oil to be reduced from its current 27 percent, along with some movement on petroleum product tariffs.

"It is obviously positive, but not too exciting for oil stocks, Shrivatsa Kumar, oil analyst at Jardine Fleming told Reuters, adding that what the sector really needed is a hike in domestic product prices.
"A price increase in petroleum products is needed to improve oil companies liquidity, he said.

The petroleum minister told local news agency Asian News International that there was no current government plan to raise state-controlled domestic prices of petroleum products to stem a backlog of payments to state-owned oil firms, projected to reach 158 billion rupees by the end of March.
The oil companies carry the burden of selling oil products to Indian consumers below world prices, and are repaid by the government later.

Oil analysts had already discounted any chance that Finance Minister P. Chidambaram would announce price increases in his budget to be announced at 1700 local (1130 GMT), and would rather opt to wait until the budget had been approved.
"Just tinkering around with customs duty will not help a lot," said Sanjeev Prasad of Kotak Securities, but he added, "It may result in some improvement of sentiment toward the sector."

However, another Bombay analyst, who requested anonymity, said he believed that if the changes in tariff rates were bold enough it could be very significant for the sector and produce a sharp bullish reaction in some oil stocks like Hindustan Petroleum Corp and Bharat Petroleum Corp.
"It is an absolute must for moving ahead with decontrol in the sector," he said. "It could be great news for a lot of these stocks, and I should imagine there will be a spurt in their prices."

The Bombay Stock Exchange was in midsession when Balu's comments were reported. HPCL stood at 381.0 rupess, up 50 paisa, BPCL was up 2.25 rupees at 367.25. The BSE will resume trading at 1800 local (1230 GMT).
